title: Angela’s Mom’s Gnocchi

items.raw: 2 pounds (about 900 g) russet potatoes, 3 or 4 large, scrubbed
About 1¼ cups (160 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
¼ cup (20 g) finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (optional)
Angela’s mom’s sauce — or 6 tablespoons butter with sage, or 3 cups tomato sauce

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F. Prick the potatoes and bake directly on the rack 50 to 60 minutes, until a knife slides through with no resistance. Baking instead of boiling keeps them dry, and dry potatoes mean light gnocchi.

Halve the potatoes while hot (use a towel) and scoop out the flesh. Pass it through a ricer or food mill onto the counter and spread it out to let the steam escape for 5 to 10 minutes. You should have about 1 pound 10 ounces (750 g) riced potato.
Sprinkle the potato with the salt and Parmesan, add the yolk, and scatter about 1 cup of the flour over the top. Gather it together with a bench scraper, folding rather than kneading.

steps.lead: Use as little flour as possible.
steps.text: Add more flour only until the dough holds together and is just barely tacky — soft, like a well-handled earlobe. More flour makes heavier gnocchi. Test one: drop a small piece into boiling salted water; if it falls apart, work in another tablespoon of flour.

Divide into 6 pieces and roll each into a rope about ¾ inch thick. Cut into ¾-inch pieces. Leave them as pillows, or roll each off the back of a fork with your thumb to make ridges that hold sauce. Set on a floured sheet pan.
Drop into a large pot of well-salted boiling water in two or three batches. They sink, then rise. Let them float for 30 seconds, then lift out with a slotted spoon.
Toss gently with the sauce in a wide pan and serve right away.

notes.label: Russets only
notes.text: waxy potatoes like Yukon Golds or red potatoes need much more flour and turn gummy.

notes.label: Don’t knead
notes.text: working the dough develops gluten and makes the gnocchi chewy. Mix only until it comes together.

notes.label: Freezing
notes.text: freeze uncooked gnocchi on the floured pan until hard, then bag. Cook from frozen; do not thaw.

notes.label: Pan-crisped
notes.text: after boiling, brown the gnocchi in butter in a hot skillet for a crisp outside.

openQuestion: Tell me about Angela’s mom — where her gnocchi come from, and when she makes them. Does she use egg or no egg? Ridged on a fork or board, or plain pillows? And what sauce does she put on them?
